=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.
exchanges.text:
## Executive view

The Seller’s package is materially seller-friendly. The “standard/cleared” labels should not be accepted as binding; several provisions affect the core allocation of title, debt, IP, tax, privacy and completion risk. The general disclosure and knowledge provisions are particularly problematic because they could convert unresolved diligence issues into assumed buyer risk.

## Material issues and push-backs

### 1. Liability limitations

Push back strongly on:

- **20% general warranty cap (AUD 4.8m):** seek a higher cap, at least 30–50% of price, with separate higher or uncapped protection for fundamental matters.
- **Fundamental/title warranties subject to the general cap and 18-month limit:** unacceptable. Title, capacity, authority, ownership and encumbrance warranties should be uncapped or subject to a cap equal to the purchase price, with a materially longer survival period.
- **All-claims limitation package:** exclusions should apply for fraud, wilful misconduct, deliberate concealment, tax, IP, privacy/data incidents, debt, leakage, specific indemnities and breaches of completion obligations.
- **De minimis of AUD25,000 and basket of AUD250,000:** seek no threshold for fundamental warranties, specific indemnities or fraud. The basket should preferably be a **tipping basket**, not a deductible basket.
- **18-month warranty period:** extend to at least 24 months. Tax claims should survive until expiry of the relevant statutory assessment/recovery period plus an agreed tail; title and IP claims should survive substantially longer or until the relevant limitation period expires.
- **Notice provisions:** failure to commence proceedings within a short period after notice should not automatically extinguish a properly notified claim.

### 2. General disclosure and buyer knowledge

Reject the proposed data-room/public-register disclosure and “knowledge” deeming provisions.

The Seller is attempting to disclose:

- every matter in DD-002 to DD-012;
- all Accounts and statutory records;
- public registers; and
- anything discoverable by the Buyer or advisers.

That is not sufficiently specific or fair disclosure. It could substantially undermine the warranties, including in relation to matters the Seller has not clearly identified as breaches.

Require that:

- general disclosure is limited to matters **fairly and specifically disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter;
- a data-room index or document dump does not constitute disclosure of all contents or implications of each document;
- public-register information is not deemed disclosed unless expressly identified;
- buyer knowledge means actual knowledge of specified senior Buyer personnel, not constructive or adviser knowledge;
- no knowledge exclusion applies to fraud, deliberate concealment, fundamental warranties or specific indemnities;
- the Seller warrants that the Disclosure Letter is complete, accurate and not misleading by omission; and
- warranties are repeated at Completion, with an obligation to update disclosures and a Buyer termination/claim right for material new matters.

### 3. Bluefen — major customer/change-of-control risk

Bluefen represents approximately 30% of FY26 revenue. There is no final consent and no evidence that conditions have been satisfied.

The Seller’s proposal is inadequate. Written consent may still be conditional, revocable or ineffective if clause 11.3 conditions remain outstanding.

Require:

- final unconditional written consent;
- evidence that every associated condition has been satisfied or waived;
- confirmation that the contract remains in full force, with no termination, repricing or adverse amendment;
- a condition precedent to Completion; and
- a termination right or price protection if consent is not obtained.

If Completion proceeds before consent, require a specific indemnity and an escrow/retention or price adjustment reflecting the customer concentration and replacement risk.

### 4. Riverlark facility and security

The company has approximately AUD3.2m outstanding, and no discharge is included. A post-Completion release is not acceptable in a debt-free/cash-free transaction.

Require at or before Completion:

- full repayment of the Riverlark facility;
- delivery of executed releases and discharges of all security;
- confirmation that no break costs, fees, guarantees, hedging liabilities or other amounts remain;
- lender releases for the Company and its assets; and
- evidence that all PPSR registrations and other security interests have been discharged.

The amount should be paid directly from the Completion funds flow or withheld from the Seller. Any unpaid amount should be treated as debt and deducted from the purchase price, with an indemnity for residual liabilities.

### 5. Ironquay IP and SOW3

The disclosure indicates that transfer of SOW3 Project Materials depends on payment of every SOW3 fee, with AUD180,000 open and no payment or assignment evidence.

The existing indemnity limited to one payment is too narrow. The Buyer may acquire a company without ownership or usable rights to important IP.

Require:

- payment or escrow of the AUD180,000;
- executed assignment or confirmation of ownership of all SOW3 Project Materials;
- all necessary moral-rights consents and third-party rights;
- warranties that the Company owns or validly licenses all required IP; and
- a specific indemnity covering all losses from the Ironquay matter, including re-performance, replacement development, licence fees, customer claims, delay and enforcement costs.

This indemnity should sit outside the general cap, de minimis, basket and ordinary warranty period, or have a separate substantial cap and survival period.

### 6. Employee completion bonuses

The AUD420,000 bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment, are omitted from the funds flow, and may attract payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.

Require the Seller to:

- pay all bonuses and employer on-costs before or at Completion;
- provide a full calculation and employee schedule;
- obtain releases or confirmations where appropriate;
- indemnify the Buyer for bonuses, payroll tax, superannuation, leave, PAYG and other employment liabilities arising from pre-Completion service or the transaction; and
- confirm there are no other transaction, retention or change-of-control payments.

The amount should be included in the Completion accounts/debt-like items or paid by the Seller separately. It must not be left as an undisclosed post-Completion liability.

### 7. Export/privacy incident

This is an unresolved potential privacy and confidentiality breach involving approximately 1,240 records. Its status and notification obligations remain unknown.

Do not accept the Seller’s characterisation as merely preliminary. Require:

- a detailed incident report and forensic investigation;
- confirmation of what data was exported, to whom, and whether it was accessed or copied;
- preservation and deletion/return confirmations;
- assessment of Privacy Act, contractual and regulatory notification obligations;
- all required notifications and remediation before Completion, where appropriate;
- customer, employee and regulator communications controls; and
- a specific indemnity for investigation, notification, remediation, credit monitoring, claims, regulatory penalties to the extent recoverable, and third-party losses.

The incident should be excluded from the general liability cap and ordinary thresholds, or given a separate meaningful cap and long survival period.

### 8. Office lease

The disclosure does not resolve whether a share sale triggers consent, notice or default under the lease.

Require:

- review of the complete lease and amendments;
- landlord confirmation or waiver if required;
- confirmation that all notices have been given and no default or termination right has arisen;
- warranty that rent, outgoings and make-good obligations are current; and
- indemnity for any pre-Completion lease breach or transaction-triggered consequence.

If consent is legally required, make it a Completion condition.

### 9. Supplier renewals

The three AUD110,000 renewals may represent AUD330,000 of commitments, but the disclosure does not explain whether they are binding, avoidable, accrued or ordinary-course.

Require a schedule stating:

- counterparty, term, renewal date and termination rights;
- services received and amounts accrued or prepaid;
- change-of-control provisions;
- whether the commitments are commercially necessary and at market rates; and
- whether any suppliers are related parties.

Any pre-Completion accrued cost should be reflected in working capital/debt adjustments or paid by the Seller. The Buyer should have termination or price protection for non-ordinary-course or undesirable commitments.

### 10. Mossvale assignment restriction

Although the disclosure says consent may not be required merely because of a share sale, that is not a substitute for contract analysis.

Require confirmation that:

- no consent or notice is required;
- the contract will not terminate or become terminable;
- no default, price increase or service reduction arises; and
- the contract remains valid after Completion.

If uncertain, obtain a waiver or make it a condition precedent.

### 11. Title to shares

The share register is useful evidence but does not establish complete title.

Require warranties and evidence covering:

- legal and beneficial ownership of all shares;
- fully paid shares;
- no options, warrants, conversion rights, trusts or nominees;
- no encumbrances, liens or third-party claims;
- no pre-emptive rights or restrictions;
- valid corporate authority and execution; and
- original share certificates, ASIC records and executed transfer documents.

These should be fundamental warranties with enhanced survival and liability protection.

### 12. Tax and IP warranties

The Seller’s assertion that tax and IP are “settled” should be rejected unless the agreed drafting actually provides adequate protection.

Require:

- a standalone tax covenant covering pre-Completion tax, payroll tax, GST, superannuation, transfer duty, employment taxes and audit liabilities;
- protection for tax arising from Completion or pre-Completion restructurings;
- robust IP warranties covering ownership, infringement, open-source software, employee/contractor assignments, registrations, licences and claims; and
- separate caps and survival periods for tax and IP.

## Completion and price mechanics

The Completion mechanics should expressly address:

1. Riverlark repayment and security releases.
2. Employee bonuses and all on-costs.
3. Ironquay payment/assignment or escrow.
4. Bluefen consent and condition satisfaction.
5. Privacy incident remediation and required notices.
6. Supplier and other transaction-related liabilities.
7. Debt-free/cash-free and working-capital adjustments.
8. No leakage or undisclosed payments between signing and Completion.
9. A completion escrow or retention for unresolved matters.

## Priority negotiation position

The highest-priority push-backs are:

1. **Riverlark:** repay and discharge at Completion; deduct from funds if necessary.
2. **Bluefen:** unconditional consent and satisfied conditions as a condition precedent.
3. **Ironquay:** secure ownership of the IP and broaden the indemnity.
4. **Employee bonuses:** Seller-funded payment and on-cost indemnity.
5. **Privacy incident:** investigation, remediation and specific indemnity.
6. **Disclosure/knowledge:** no blanket data-room disclosure or constructive knowledge.
7. **Fundamental warranties:** outside the general cap and 18-month period.
8. **Tax/IP:** standalone protections.
9. **Completion funds flow:** include all identified liabilities and require a full debt-like item schedule.
10. **Supplier, lease and Mossvale contracts:** confirm continuity and obtain consents or waivers where required.

The proposed package should not be treated as “balanced” merely because the Seller labels certain provisions standard or settled. The unresolved disclosures indicate several risks that should either be cured before Completion, priced into the transaction, or protected by specific indemnities and escrow/retention arrangements.
